assignment.review_focus: MATRIX-003 — Software lifecycle traceability for PT9L. Verify that software requirements, architecture/design documents, unit and integration test records, software validation records, and the software traceability matrix are mutually consistent and all scoped to PT9L. Specifically investigate: (1) BP3L software diagrams appearing in the main PT9L software design folder and/or the T1 sample subfolder — determine whether these are shared-component references with documented rationale or erroneous inclusions; (2) whether the software version identifier in test records matches the version in the design document and the released BOM; (3) whether Bluetooth software requirements are traced to test cases and validation evidence; (4) whether any software document header, footer, or internal reference cites PT9C, PT3SBT, or BP3L as the primary product model without justification.

input_package.goal: Check software requirements, design, tests, validation, traceability, versioning, and legacy software artifact references.
input_package.system_prompt: Review software lifecycle consistency using only supplied evidence IDs.

primary_scope_rules: PT9L is the target product model for this DHF
Documents in '2L风险改 - 历史文件' folder are explicitly historical
Documents referencing PT2L, PT3SBT, BP3L, or PT9C outside clearly marked historical/draft folders require justification

key_entities.product_description: 红外非接触式额头温度计 (Infrared No-Touch Forehead Thermometer)
key_entities.intended_use: Intermittent measurement of body temperature from forehead skin surface on people of all ages; consumer home use and healthcare provider use
key_entities.bluetooth: PT9L can transmit temperature to smart device with Bluetooth (per Risk Management Report)

regulatory_baseline: EN ISO 80601-2-56:2017+A1:2018 (EU, applicability differs between draft and final design input)
MDR 2017/745 (EU, applicability differs between draft and final design input)

candidate_discovery_hints: PT9C appears as a sub-component PCB document number and as a standalone product in clinical evaluation and user test documents
PT3SBT appears in design output list two and a label review document filed under T1 sample folder
BP3L software diagrams appear in both the main software design folder and T1 sample subfolder
PT2L risk documents are in a '历史文件' subfolder but one (F0013) carries a PT9L document number internally

mandatory_audit_matrix.check_goal: Verify that software requirements, design, test records, validation, and traceability records are consistent.

assignment.review_focus: MATRIX-003 — Software lifecycle traceability for PT9L. Verify that software requirements, architecture/design documents, unit and integration test records, software validation records, and the software traceability matrix are mutually consistent and all scoped to PT9L. Specifically investigate: (1) BP3L software diagrams appearing in the main PT9L software design folder and/or the T1 sample subfolder — determine whether these are shared-component references with documented rationale or erroneous inclusions; (2) whether the software version identifier in test records matches the version in the design document and the released BOM; (3) whether Bluetooth software requirements are traced to test cases and validation evidence; (4) whether any software document header, footer, or internal reference cites PT9C, PT3SBT, or BP3L as the primary product model without justification.

agent_runs.summary: Cross-corpus scan of the PT9L DHF/DMR package reveals 14 candidate consistency issues spanning legacy product residue in active documents, document-number mismatches, unsigned approvals, wrong-product references in BOM and label documents, regulatory applicability conflicts, software diagram contamination, and blood-pressure-specific language appearing in a thermometer DHF.

Hardware audit of PT9L DHF/DMR reveals five substantive consistency findings: a blood-pressure residue phrase in the battery design-verification plan/report, an unresolved BOM conflict between PT3-P10 dual-spring and PT5-M02/M03 separate springs, a total-assembly drawing part-number anomaly (T-Z1-P10 used for two distinct PCBs), missing pass/fail verdicts in multiple T1 sample review checklists, and object-temperature mode accuracy tolerance (±0.2 °C) applied at 30 °C and 45 °C in software test plans despite the design-input accuracy specification only requiring ±0.2 °C for ≥35 °C and ≤42 °C.

The PT9L risk management file set contains multiple traceability chain breaks: the current Risk Management Report references document number PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 while the active risk set has been revised to V2.0; the active Risk Management Plan carries document number IFT-FXJH01 rather than PT9L-FXJH01; F0013 (PT2L risk plan) internally carries a PT9L-series document number creating a product-identity conflict; no evidence of Bluetooth-specific hazard verification is present in the supplied corpus; DFMEA files (F0071, F0074) are not cross-referenced to the ISO 14971 risk assessment; and the design verification plan/report cites only PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 while the current report is V2.0, leaving the closed-loop confirmation potentially misaligned.

llm_output.summary: PT9L software lifecycle audit reveals five substantive findings: BP3L software diagrams appear in the primary PT9L software design folder and T1 sample subfolder without documented shared-component rationale; the software design document version identifier (E0 23.11) cannot be reconciled with the V1.0 identifier cited in test/validation records and BOM; no Bluetooth software requirements or corresponding test/validation evidence is present in the supplied corpus; the IEC 60601-1 test report references software design document DN:PT9L-RJFA01 V1.0 which does not appear in the evidence catalog; and a label review document filed under the active T1 sample folder carries PT2L as the primary product model without justification.

findings.claim: The software design documents use version identifier 'E0 23.11' while the operation guide, BOM, and IEC 60601-1 test report all use 'V1.0', and no version mapping or equivalence record is present in the supplied evidence to reconcile these two identifiers.
findings.rationale: SW-001 and SW-017 title the software diagram as 'BP3L 软件图样E0 23.11', using the 'E0 23.11' versioning scheme. SW-013 states 'Version 1.0' and SW-014 states 'Software version: V1.0' in the PT9L operation guide (F0083). SW-015 and SW-016 reference 'PT9C-CNTP01 V1.0' in the BOM, using the V-series scheme. SW-064 through SW-067 in the IEC 60601-1 test report cite 'Software design solutions DN:PT9L-RJFA01 V1.0' as the evidence for PEMS development lifecycle compliance. No document in the catalog maps 'E0 23.11' to 'V1.0' or explains whether these are parallel versioning schemes for different artifact types or a genuine mismatch. IEC 62304 and IEC 60601-1 clause 14 require that software version identifiers be unambiguous and traceable across lifecycle artifacts.
challenge_questions: What is the relationship between the 'E0 23.11' version designation used in the software diagram and the 'V1.0' designation used in the operation guide and test report — are these the same software release?
Is there a software version control table or release note that maps document revision codes (e.g., E0) to software version numbers (e.g., V1.0)?

Does the released BOM (PT9L-EBOM01 V1.0 and PT9L-T1EB01 V1.0) reference the software version that was validated, and can the traceability from BOM software version to validated software version be demonstrated?
